content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim in turn: first, that the shop was slow for users during the outage, and that this is what a reader would notice. Next, that the likely cause was the system repeatedly removing the extra servers it had just added. The third sentence about a wait-related setting is a separate point, so I'll see whether it belongs with the cause or stands alone.

I'm now weighing whether the sentence about the setting being zero belongs with the likely cause. The config file reading of zero seems to be a checked fact, but the step about too few servers is still part of the causal chain, so I'm judging whether the hedge covers the whole sentence.

I'm going through the remaining claims one by one: the Argus cost estimate, the fact that nobody was paged, the raised minimum server count that is still in place with sync left off, and the proposed fix that is still a draft and has not been applied. Each of those lines up with what the record shows.

supported.quote: For {duration}, the io-shop online shop responded to requests far more slowly than usual.
rows: What a reader saw: Shop requests responded far more slowly than usual

supported.quote: The likely cause was the shop's automatic scaling repeatedly taking away extra servers it had just added.
rows: Why, in plain words: The shop's automatic scaling likely kept taking away the extra servers it had just added

supported.quote: A setting meant to make it wait before scaling back down was set so that it did not wait, which left too few servers to answer requests quickly.
rows: Why, in plain words: ... because a setting meant to make it wait before scaling back down was set to zero, and that left too few servers to answer requests quickly

supported.quote: Argus estimates the cost to the shop in lost takings at {customer_loss}.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, so no on-call staff were called out.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one

supported.quote: To end the slowdown, Argus raised the minimum number of servers the shop keeps running.
That change is confirmed and still in place, and automatic syncing of the shop's settings has been left switched off.
rows: Argus: raised the autoscaler floor of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off

supported.quote: Argus has also proposed a fix, which is open as a draft and has not been applied.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #544 - opened as a draft
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its fix
The record holds nothing about it after that.
